15:Wrap heavy steps in `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=3G`. Downloads are cached; the scripts are idempotent. Peak memory is about 250 MB and each step runs in under 30 s once the cache is filled.
28:- `carr_lon_deg, carr_lat_deg`: sunpy `HeliographicCarrington` with `observer="earth"`. This applies the conventional Earth-observer light-time definition of the Carrington meridian, so all bodies share one rotating frame at each time. Using `observer="self"` instead would shift the comet by about 0.07 deg.
118:| hourly_maven | 28% | 4/23 | ends 2025-12-05T23:59 (CDAWeb stop date) |
130:  - SolO PAS reproduces SolO COHO with median ratio 1.000; the 5–95% ratio range is within ±0.8% in n and +0.3% in v.
134:- ACE K1 against Wind H1 for the same hour: v ratio 0.996, but the median n ratio is 0.66, with 5–95% range 0.23–0.96. The preprint scaled ACE n by a fixed factor of 1.7, which corresponds to a ratio of 0.59.
The local log contains an empty or redacted thinking block; plaintext is unavailable.

{
  "message": "All five tasks are done. The ephemerides pass every frame check. Cross-checked against the preprint caches, my hourly series agree to within 1%. The big gap: no in-situ heavy-ion composition from any spacecraft is public for Oct–Dec 2025.

Root: /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/claude/data/

**Files written**
- `ephem/<body>.csv`, hourly from 2025-10-01 to 12-20, columns as you asked plus `ecl_lat_deg`. One file each for 3i_atlas, earth, stereo_a, solar_orbiter, parker_solar_probe, bepicolombo, mars, maven, venus, mercury, juice, psyche, europa_clipper. I also added ace and wind.
- `ephem/comet_geometry_mid.json` and `ephem/frame_checks.json`.
- `insitu/` per-product CSVs:
  - omni_hro2_5min, omni2_mrg1hr
  - stereo_a_pla_1dmax_1min, stereo_a_magplasma_1min, stereo_a_coho1hr
  - solar_orbiter_pas_grnd_mom_1min, solar_orbiter_mag_rtn_1min, solar_orbiter_coho1hr
  - parker_solar_probe_spi_sf00_l3_mom_1min, parker_solar_probe_mag_rtn_1min
  - ace_swe_k1, ace_mfi_h1
  - wind_swe_h1
  - maven_insitu_kp_upstream_1min
- `insitu/hourly_{omni,wind,ace,stereo_a,solar_orbiter,parker_solar_probe,maven}.csv`, columns `utc,n,v,T,B,vr`, plus `na_np` (alpha/proton ratio) for omni, wind and ace.
  - Bins are [HH:00, HH+1), labeled HH:30, on a complete grid; a value is kept only with at least 50% time coverage.
  - Products faster than 1 min (SolO PAS at 1–4 s, PSP SPAN-I, MAVEN at 4 s) were first reduced to 1-min means.
- `qc/`: trajectories_hci_xy.png, timeseries_n_v_flux.png, coverage.png, crosscheck_preprint.{png,json}.
- `README.md`, `inventory.json`, `scripts/` (9 scripts), and `raw/` (Horizons text, gzipped HAPI chunks, CDAWeb master CDFs; about 140 MB).

Other agents' folders sit inside data/ (adapt, boundary, cme, gong, hmi, ips, wsa_ccmc, scripts_rs, and extra files in qc/). I left them alone, and README.md and inventory.json describe only my products.

**Comet at mid-observation, 2025-12-03T23:08:00.5 UTC**
- r = 1.8734 AU
- HGI lon/lat 71.02 / −6.45°
- Carrington lon/lat 23.53 / −6.45° (sunpy HGC, observer = Earth)
- HEEQ lon/lat 75.06 / −6.45°
- Ecliptic J2000 lon/lat 146.91 / +0.41°
- HCI velocity (60.60, 24.22, −7.01) km/s, |v| = 65.64
  - Radial +43.13 km/s, tangential 49.48 km/s.
  - The tangential part is −49.43 in longitude (retrograde) and +2.17 northward.

| Separation (comet − body) | HGI | Ecliptic |
|---|---|---|
| Earth | +75.06° | +75.22° |
| STEREO-A | +24.95° | +24.84° |
| SolO | +60.55° | +61.95° |
| PSP | +152.81° | +152.94° |
| Mars | −120.78° | −120.60° |

- Positive means the comet is east of the body.
- Under pure corotation, structure seen at STEREO-A reaches the comet's longitude 1.76 d later; for Earth it is 5.29 d.
- STEREO-A's latitude (−5.36°) is close to the comet's.

**Frame checks**
- HCI latitude matches Horizons IAU_SUN body-equator output to 1e-14°; the longitude offset is a constant −61.1005°, as expected from the two frames' axis definitions.
- Carrington longitude matches the Horizons sub-observer point to 3e-6° for Earth. STEREO-A, SolO and PSP differ by 0.003–0.08°, which is their light-time difference from Earth.
- Ecliptic tracks reproduce the preprint's cached tracks to 2e-6°.

**Coverage, Nov 15–Dec 10 (valid hourly n; XMM window = 23 hourly bins)**

| Series | Coverage | XMM window | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| OMNI hourly / OMNI2 | 95% / 99% | 23/23 | |
| Wind H1 | 55% | 16/23 | no data Nov 25–30 |
| ACE K1 | 100% | 23/23 | |
| STEREO-A | 97% | 23/23 | |
| SolO | 89% | 23/23 | |
| PSP | 10% | 0/23 | plasma only Dec 7 10:30–Dec 19 07:30; B 60% |
| MAVEN upstream | 28% | 4/23 | ends Dec 5 |

**Cross-check against the preprint caches**
- The same products are identical: SolO COHO, ACE K1 and OMNI2 have Δ = 0. STEREO-A COHO differs by at most 0.05 cm⁻³ and 0.5 km/s, likely a reprocessing since the cache was made.
- STEREO-A PLASTIC 1-min, binned from each COHO tag forward, reproduces COHO to |Δn| ≤ 0.005.
- SolO PAS reproduces SolO COHO with ratio 1.000 (5–95% within ±0.8% in n).
- This confirms COHO time tags mark the start of the hour. The preprint treated them as sample times while using hour-centered OMNI2 tags, a 30-min inconsistency that is minor.
- OMNI_HRO2 hourly against the cached OMNI2 has ratio 1.000.
- Unshifted Wind H1 matches OMNI2 best at a +1 h lag (r(log n) = 0.995), which is OMNI's propagation shift to the bow-shock nose.
- ACE K1 density against Wind: median ratio 0.66 (5–95% 0.23–0.96), while speeds agree (0.996). The preprint's fixed factor of 1.7 corresponds to 0.59.

**Missing or surprising**
- **No composition data.** ACE SWICS ends 2025-03-16 (on CDAWeb and at the ACE Science Center). SolO HIS L3 ends 2023-04 (on CDAWeb and ESA SOAR). STEREO-A Fe charge states end in 2011. The only composition proxy is the alpha/proton ratio.
- **ACE:** level-2 SWEPAM ends 2024-07, so only preliminary K1 exists, and its densities read low with deep dropouts. Use ACE for speed and timing, not absolute density.
- **OMNI** in this period is 100% Wind (ID 52), so it adds no independent spacecraft. DSCOVR plasma is not on CDAWeb after 2019.
- **STEREO-A PLASTIC 2025 files** have no RTN velocities, no E/W flow angle and no caution flag. Requesting any of them makes HAPI return "no data", so `vr` is NaN for STEREO-A (and for ACE); use `v`.
- **PSP:**
  - SPC has no data.
  - Outside encounter (0.4–0.7 AU), SPAN-I densities are about 0.1–2 cm⁻³, roughly 10× too low, so I masked hourly plasma where r > 0.3 AU.
  - Perihelion is 2025-12-13 ~07 UT at 0.0459 AU.
- **SolO PAS:**
  - `quality_factor` is undocumented, so I kept it as a column but did not filter on it.
  - I rejected samples missing N, V or T, which matches COHO.
  - Data gaps: Oct 17 22:06–Oct 24 07:00 and Dec 5–6.
- **MAVEN:**
  - I used the KP 4-s product because it carries positions.
  - Upstream means outside 1.2× the Vignes (2000) bow shock, with good-quality density, an antisunward flow faster than 200 km/s, and T < 1e6 K.
  - Temperatures are biased high (median about 2e5 K) because the onboard moments assume pure protons.
  - A density spike to 50–125 cm⁻³ on Oct 29 is kept as possibly real.
- **BepiColombo** is 21° and Mercury 7° from the comet in HGI longitude, both at about 0.35 AU, but no BepiColombo data are public."
}
